course_name_original: Métodos avanzados de cálculo en ingeniería mecánica
course_name_en: Advanced Calculation Methods in Mechanical Engineering
prerequisites: Elasticity and Strength of Materials II

learning_outcomes.text: Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Knowledge and capabilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Capacity for information management, handling and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of the finite element method
Variational formulation of the bar element
Variational formulation of the beam element
Variational formulation of the plane element
Isoparametric formulation of the plane element
Formulation of plate and Shell elements
teaching_methods: Expositive classes in large groups: Lectures
Expositive classes in large groups: Presentation of theory and general examples
Expositive classes in large groups: Introductory activities
Expositive classes in large groups: Others
Classes in practice groups: Computer labs
Classes in practice groups: Practical activities

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (Written theoretical-practical exam)
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises (Completion and presentation of assignments)
Laboratory/field practices/use of ICT tools (Attendance at practical classes and preparation of report)

assessment_rules: The grading system is governed by RD 1125/2003. Evaluation consists of a fundamental exam (60%), attendance and participation (5%), laboratory practice reports (20%), and a proposed assignment (15%). Attendance and submission of practice reports and the assignment are mandatory. A minimum grade of 3 out of 10 is required for each practice report and 5 out of 10 for the assignment. Failure to submit mandatory components on time results in failure of the course. Students may request a single evaluation (100% exam) under exceptional circumstances as per Article 13 of the University of Jaén's Academic and Evaluation Regulations, with the request made during the teaching period.
